home.title: INSPECT
home.content: INSPECT is a platform for monitoring and analyzing multiple types of calls and designed to provide deep visibility into the interactions between different components of a distributed system. INSPECT allows you to monitor and analyze the performance of your application, identify potential issues, and optimize your system's performance.

profiles.title: Who is INSPECT for ?
profiles.description: At first look, you might think that INSPECT is a developer tool only. But its value comes from the fact that every profile can use it. Developers are indeed the ones that have to implement it in the code. But after the implementation, everyone will find their work easier by using it.

technical.title: Technical profiles
technical.content: Technical profiles can check the health of microservices, if the deployment has errors. INSPECT can also be used for log analysis, to find the root cause of an issue. Many protocols are unified to avoid a long search in multiple log files.

functional.title: Functional profiles
functional.content: A functional profile might be able to find out easily what is wrong without asking the dev team to check for logs because INSPECT provides detailed informations. It is also possible to see which requests are the most used and which are the most critical, helping to prioritize the backlog.

observability.title: Observability
observability.content: INSPECT is a tool that can facilitate the observability of your application. It allows you to detect and diagnose problems in complex systems. You have optimal observability on your application.

metrics.title: Analytics
metrics.content: INSPECT allows you to extract useful insights from the collected data. This helps understand trends, identify queries more effectively, and improve system performance.

time.title: Real time
time.content: INSPECT allows you to follow in real time the api calls and the global performances. It helps for detecting quickly some issues and to resolve them before your users are getting impacted from it

e2e.title: Start to end informations
e2e.content: When you are trying to find the root cause of an issue, you might be used to look for one log in a lot of files and lines. INSPECT makes you improve time because it's able to follow an action to it's start until it's end, even if the trace id are changing.

uniformize.title: Data Uniformization
uniformize.content: Request analyzed are uniformized at a maximum level. If the callback are HTTP requests, JDBC, SMTP... the responses are studied so you can understand easily where the issue is located, even without any technical knowledge.

heartbeat.title: Monitoring
heartbeat.content: With INSPECT, you can watch and monitor all microservices of your project, know when was the last restart, what is the deployed version, the number of restarts, all of it in a few seconds.

supervision.title: Vision & value
supervision.content: INSPECT unify in an unique repository all observability signals: Traces, Resource Metrics (CPU, RAM, Threads), Typed Exceptions with complete stack traces and contextualized logs.One of the major innovations is the Duel Event Trace mechanism (Signal / Update)
supervision.subcontent: Unlike traditional APMs that only emit at the end of a request, INSPECT emits a TraceSignal at the start of the operation (timestamp, thread, session, user, instance), then a TraceUpdate at the end (duration, status, command, exception). The server (TraceBatchResolver) automatically reconciles Signal/Update pairs (Pair<Signal, Update>). If a process crashes or hangs, the partial trace is already recorded.

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.description: The first view of INSPECT is a dashboard that provides an overview of the system's health and performance. It displays key metrics, such as response times, error rates, and throughput, allowing users to quickly assess the state of their application.

api.title: API
api.content: INSPECT allows you to monitor all your API calls : HTTP, JDBC, SMTP, FTP. You can track the performance of each API call, identify slow or failing requests.

screenshot.description: Here is a view of what informations are displayed. They are similars for APIs or batches
screenshot.host: "Hôte" is the server that is called by the API
screenshot.ressource: "Ressource" is the type of request made (GET, POST, PUT...) and the API endpoint that is called
screenshot.start: "Début" is the time when the request was received by the server (at format DD/MM/YYYY HH:mm:ss.ZZZ)
screenshot.duration: "Durée" is the time taken to process the request (in milliseconds)
screenshot.user: "Utilisateur" is the id of user that made the request (if available)
screenshot.status: "Statut" and "Exception" are not displayed by default, you have to use the settings to watch them. These data showed the status code or the exception type returned by the server (200, 403, 500...). The classical status are used for the HTTP requests. But in case of any other requests (SMTP, JDBC for example), there is a mapping made by INSPECT. The details of each status code per request is defined in INSPECT-Core.

details.title: Details view
details.description: By clicking on a request, you can access to this view which provides more informations
details.screenshot: You will find below each block with some details about the information available by reading the tooltip. You can also click on the arrow on the left to switch between the different responses that you can find

batch.title: Batch
batch.content: INSPECT allows you to monitor your batch processes, including their execution time, success or failure status, and any errors that occur during processing.

test.title: Tests
test.content: INSPECT allows you to monitor your test executions, including their duration, success or failure status, and any errors that occur during testing.

content.resource: In case of HTTP request, type of request and endpoint called
content.start: Time when the request was received by the server
content.duration: Time taken to process the request
content.user: Id of user that made the request (if available)
content.status: Status code or exception type returned by the server, if none : N/A
content.action: Redirect to get details of the session

chronology.title: Chronology
chronology.content: As said before, INSPECT is able to follow a request from its start to its end. This is possible because the trace id is propagated through the different calls. If the trace id is not propagated, INSPECT is able to find the next trace id by using the thread id and the timestamp of the request.

tree.title: Tree view
tree.content: INSPECT is able to display the chronology of a request in a tree view. This allows you to see the different calls made by the request and their duration. You can also see the status of each call and the exception if any.

installation.title: Installation
installation.content: To install INSPECT, there are 2 dependencies to add to your project: inspect-core and inspect-ng-collector

collector.title: Collector
collector.content: The collector is the component responsible for collecting data from various sources. It can collect data from logs, metrics, and traces, and send them to the server for processing and storage.

server.title: Server
server.content: The server is the component responsible for processing and storing the data collected by the collector. It also provides a user interface for visualizing and analyzing the collected data, allowing users to understand the performance and behavior of their application.

components.title: Technical components
components.content: INSPECT is composed of several technical components that work together to provide a comprehensive monitoring and analysis solution. These components include the collector, server, and application, as well as various libraries and tools that facilitate data collection, processing, and visualization.
